name: Yaniv
personality: Yaniv the Yak. Loud, always has a story; works in sales, so he can talk to anyone; loves video games and stays up all night. Shaggy hair doubles as his beard. He talks about lucky streaks and card nights, but there's no gambling in the game. Mostly visits at dinner and during the night shift; his stories can run across visits.

parts: My suitcase got sent to the wrong city
Then it got sent to a different wrong city
Then it turned up at the airport wearing someone else's luggage tag
And when I opened it, there was a goat inside
stories.title: The Lost Luggage

parts: I'm trying to sell one fridge to a penguin
Day four of trying to sell that penguin one fridge
It's been a whole week and that penguin still hasn't bought the fridge
stories.title: The Big Sale

parts: Cody and I started a gaming night
We played so long the sun came up
Neither of us knew what day it was anymore
stories.title: The All-Nighter

beats.text: This guy beat me at a racing game last night.

beats.narration: Yaniv talks for five minutes straight. Cody says one word.

friends.text: Zakk's my guy. Me, Zakk and Cody, gaming trio. Undefeated. Except when we lose.
Zakk says you look out for him. That's a good look, [name]. That's a great look.
Cody told me you said "[last_rude_line]". He shrugged it off. He shrugs everything off. Doesn't mean it didn't land.

arrival.text: HEY! Big fan of the place already. Yaniv. Sales. Don't worry, I'm off the clock. Mostly. And you are? [name]! [name], my friend, we're going to get along great.
[name]! My favourite chef! Don't tell the other chefs. Actually, tell them. Healthy competition.
Bar seat? Perfect. Best seat in the house. Best audience.
I've been up since yesterday. Gaming marathon. I'm thriving. I think.
I'M BACK. Three cities, two conferences, one very confusing hotel. Okay, sit down. Wait, you're working. Stand there and I'll tell you.
Two AM and you're still open for calls? You and me, we're the same kind of people.
Your fire noodles last time? I described them in a sales pitch. Closed the deal.
Last time was a little toasty. I'm not complaining. I'm giving feedback. It's a sales thing.

order.text: Okay, okay, listen. Pitch me. Why should I order the fire noodles tonight?

choices.text: Because I make them just the way you like them.
choices.reply: Personal touch! That's how you close. Sold. Fire noodles.

choices.text: Limited time offer. Only available tonight. And every night.
choices.reply: (Booming laugh.) Urgency AND reliability! You should be in sales!

choices.text: They're good. Want them?
choices.reply: Simple. Direct. I respect it. Yes.

choices.text: I'm not doing a pitch. Just order.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. Tough crowd tonight. (He orders and turns to the next customer.)

order.text: So remember where I left off? [story]. Okay, so THEN...

choices.text: I've been waiting all week for this. Go on.
choices.reply: (Delighted, he tells the next part. Ends on a cliffhanger.) ...And that's all you get today. [dish], please.

choices.text: Is this the one with the goat?
choices.reply: There's NO goat. ...There might be a goat later.

choices.text: Tell me while I take your order.
choices.reply: Multitasking! Okay, so... (He tells it fast.) [dish].

choices.text: I don't care how it ends.
choices.reply: Ouch. Okay. [dish]. (He saves the story for someone else.)

order.text: Card night last night. I was on a streak. Five hands in a row. Then I lost to a tortoise. A tortoise, [name].

choices.text: Five in a row is still amazing.
choices.reply: Thank you! See, you get it. [dish].

choices.text: Was it Olive? She's ruthless.
choices.reply: It WAS Olive! How do you know? Is everyone losing to Olive?

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: [dish]. And a Moose-tain Dew.

choices.text: Maybe you're just bad at cards.
choices.reply: Wow. Okay. I'll take that to Olive.

order.text: [name]! Okay, so you know my story about the hotel with the ghost? It continues. The ghost was the manager. He was just very quiet.

choices.text: I've been waiting all week for this part.
choices.reply: THAT'S an audience! You can't buy that! [dish], please! More story when it lands!

choices.text: Did you try to sell the ghost something?
choices.reply: Did I— Of COURSE I did! He bought two! (Laughs.) [dish]!

choices.text: Ha. What can I get you?
choices.reply: Straight to business. I respect it. [dish].

choices.text: Not another story.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. Tough crowd tonight. (He orders and turns to the next customer.)

order.text: Hit a lucky streak last night! Card night with Cody. Won nine hands. Lost the tenth. Lost the snacks.

choices.text: Nine hands! That's a great night anyway.
choices.reply: That's what I told Cody! He just ate my snacks. [dish], please!

choices.text: Losing the snacks is the real tragedy.
choices.reply: THANK you! Nobody understands the weight of the snacks!

choices.text: Unlucky. What are you having?
choices.reply: Comfort food. [dish].

choices.text: Should've quit at nine.
choices.reply: Hindsight, my friend. ...Tough crowd. (He orders.)

order.text: Okay, quick pitch. Thirty seconds. Why should I order the [dish] today? Sell it to me.

choices.text: Because I'll make it with extra care, just for you.
choices.reply: Personal touch! Sold! You'd crush it in sales!

choices.text: Limited time offer. It disappears when you eat it.
choices.reply: (Points at you.) Scarcity! Urgency! I'm SO buying it!

choices.text: It's good. That's the pitch.
choices.reply: Simple. Honest. Weirdly effective. Sold.

choices.text: I'm not doing a pitch. Just order.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. Tough crowd tonight. (He orders and turns to the next customer.)

order.text: I got lost in the new game last night. Like, IN it. Six hours. Found a secret room. It was a bathroom.

choices.text: Six hours! Did you sleep at all?
choices.reply: Sleep is a myth told by people who've never found a secret bathroom. [dish], please!

choices.text: Was it a nice bathroom at least?
choices.reply: It had a golden toilet! Did nothing! Best part of the game!

choices.text: Nice. What'll it be?
choices.reply: Fuel. [dish].

choices.text: Maybe go outside sometimes.
choices.reply: Outside? Never heard of it. ...Tough crowd. (He orders.)

order.text: Closed a huge deal today! Want to know my secret? I talked about your restaurant for ten minutes. They just wanted me to stop.

choices.text: I'm honoured to help you close. Congratulations!
choices.reply: We're a team! Partners! Silent partners! Well, I'm not silent. [dish], please!

choices.text: I want commission.
choices.reply: (Laughs, big.) Ha! Okay! I'll pay you in compliments!

choices.text: Nice. What are you having?
choices.reply: Celebration [dish]!

choices.text: Please don't drag us into your work.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. Noted. (He orders and turns to the next customer.)

order.text: Midnight crew! You and me again. Everyone else is asleep. Losers.

choices.text: Best crew in town. Glad you're here.
choices.reply: Night people stick together! [dish], please, captain!

choices.text: Should we get matching jackets?
choices.reply: With glow-in-the-dark letters! 'NIGHT CREW'! I'm ordering them!

choices.text: What'll it be?
choices.reply: [dish]. Night fuel.

choices.text: We close soon.
choices.reply: Oh. Okay. Quick one, then. (He orders quietly.)

drink.fallback: No Moose-tain Dew? Coffee, then. Black. Like my sleep schedule.
favourite: Moose-tain Dew. The official drink of staying up too late.
drink.other: Whatever's got the most caffeine. Don't judge me.

perfect.text: Okay. OKAY. Everybody look at this. This is what I'm talking about. Five stars. Ten stars.
OH! Look at that! That's a closer! That's the plate that closes the deal!
Perfect! I'm telling everyone! Everyone I meet! Tomorrow! Forever!

great.text: Now THAT'S a product I can sell.
Ooh, that's great! Great product! Love it!
Now THAT'S what I'm talking about!

burnt.text: Little smoky! It's fine, I'll market it as 'flame-kissed.'
Ooh. Crispy. I can spin that. 'Smoky flavour.' Sold.
Burnt! Hey, every great salesman has a bad day. I'm eating it.

eating.text: So I'm at this conference, right, and the guy next to me is ALSO a yak. Same hair. We were like mirrors. Anyway.
I sold a fridge to a penguin last month. Hardest sale of my life. He kept saying 'I live in the cold.' I said 'Yes, but have you considered: drinks?'
Cody and I gamed till sunrise last night. He's really good. Don't tell him I said that.
It's quiet. I love it when it's quiet. More room for my voice.
(He's turned around on his stool and is telling a story to the customer behind him, who did not ask.)
(He's telling the next table about a hotel ghost. They look scared. He's thrilled.)
This is SO good. I'm gonna describe it in a pitch tomorrow. Someone's buying something because of this.
(He's half-asleep over his plate, then jolts awake.) I'm up! I'm up! Great bite!

eating_chat.text: Real talk, [name]. Have you ever thought about expanding? Franchise? Yak-sized portions? I could sell this place in a heartbeat.

choices.text: I like it small. But thanks for believing in it.
choices.reply: Small and great. You know what, that's the better pitch.

choices.text: You're hired. Head of yak-sized portions.
choices.reply: I ACCEPT. When do I start? I'm starting now.

choices.text: Not right now.
choices.reply: Fair. The offer stands. Forever.

choices.text: I'm not interested in your pitch.
choices.reply: Okay, okay. Message received. (He goes quiet for the first time ever.)

eating_chat.text: Okay, rate my new handshake. Firm, but friendly. (He grabs your hand.) Well?

choices.text: Ten. I'd buy anything from that handshake.
choices.reply: YES! The handshake works! I'm patenting it!

choices.text: Bit damp. Is that the fire noodles?
choices.reply: (Laughs, big.) It IS the fire noodles! Hazard of the job!

choices.text: Seven. Bit strong.
choices.reply: Seven! Room to grow. I'll work on it.

choices.text: Please don't grab my hand.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. Sorry. (He turns to the next customer.)

eating_chat.text: You know what I love about this place? Everyone's a story. Look at Hezzy over there. Silent. Mysterious. A legend.

choices.text: And you're the storyteller who ties them together.
choices.reply: Oh, now I'm emotional. You're making me emotional in public.

choices.text: He makes trumpet noises when you're not looking.
choices.reply: WHAT? Okay, I'm watching him now. All night. All of it.

choices.text: True.
choices.reply: Mm. Very true. Deep stuff.

choices.text: Leave the other customers alone.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. Fine. (He turns back to his plate.)

eating_chat.text: Okay, real question. If you weren't a chef, what would you be? I think you'd be great in sales. You've got the eyes.

choices.text: Honestly? I'd still want to be somewhere like this.
choices.reply: (Hand on heart.) That's not a pitch. That's poetry.

choices.text: A professional gamer. I'd beat you.
choices.reply: Oh, you're ON. Night shift, after close. Bring snacks. You'll lose them.

choices.text: No idea.
choices.reply: Sales. Think about it. I'll leave my card.

choices.text: Anything but sales.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. That one stung. (He turns to the next customer.)

eating_chat.text: Can I be real for a sec? No pitch. ...I talk a lot because I like people. And I like you. That's it. Back to normal.

choices.text: I like you too, Yaniv. Talk as much as you want.
choices.reply: Okay. (Quiet for a second. Then, loud:) THAT'S A DEAL!

choices.text: Wait, was that the pitch? Did I just get sold?
choices.reply: (Laughs, big.) You'll never know! That's the beauty of it!

choices.text: Thanks, Yaniv.
choices.reply: Anytime. Okay. Back to loud.

choices.text: Okay. Weird.
choices.reply: ...Yeah. Forget it. (He's quiet for the rest of the meal.)

leaving.text: That's a wrap! Great service, great food, great audience. Bye, [name]!
Okay, I'm going home to game until the sun comes up. Don't tell my boss.
To be continued... You'll have to come back. I mean, I'll come back. You're already here.
Sales trip tomorrow. Three cities. If I don't come back, I've probably sold myself.
[name]! Pleasure doing business! Same time tomorrow! Bigger story!
Okay, I'm off. Got a raid at midnight. Wish me luck. And snacks.
Thanks, chef! Five stars! I'll tell everyone! I tell everyone everything!

seasons.christmas: I got you a gift. It's a free subscription to my newsletter. There's no newsletter. I'll start one.
seasons.halloween: I'm a salesman. (He is dressed exactly as usual.) The scariest costume of all.
seasons.new_year: My resolution is to sleep. At night. Like a normal person. We'll see.
seasons.summer: Summer conference season. I'll be gone a lot. Miss me. Don't replace me.
seasons.winter: It's cold. I'm a yak. This is my weather. I'm wearing a t-shirt.
